subject: Post-call: InstaLedger TTFT probing and chunk cadence alignment
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Lee <sam@instaledger.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-22T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: InstaLedger TTFT probing and chunk cadence alignment

Hi Sam — great chat earlier. Quick written recap so we have a shared checklist and clear next steps.

Call summary (high level):
- Goal: make interactive ledger search feel instantaneous for end users. Primary metric is Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) for short prompt patterns (UI button -> first byte).
- Your initial target: median TTFT ~50–60ms, p95 <= 130ms for payloads under ~256 tokens. SSE preferred for streaming UI, fallback to WebSocket if necessary.
- Typical session pattern you described: many short, chat-like requests (100–300 tokens) with synchronous UX; occasional bursts when 10–12 users run batch exports simultaneously.

What we captured as constraints to qualify pilot:
- Steady-state concurrency: 150–250 rps during business hours.
- Burst plan: spikes up to ~1,200 rps for 2–5 min during scheduled syncs (we'll simulate).
- Chunk/cadence expectation: you prefer smaller, frequent chunks — you mentioned wanting visual token flow ~25–50ms cadence.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) We (Redwood) will propose a pilot runbook and target SLOs for a short probe (see proposed buckets below).
2) Please share a sample load CSV (endpoint+payload sizes), and an ops contact that can provision a service account for the pilot.
3) We'll propose an SSE-first streaming configuration; if your CDNs or proxies block long-polling, we'll switch to WebSocket fallback.
4) Schedule: can we run a 4-hour pilot window next week? Marcus: propose Tue or Wed afternoon (PDT).

Proposed SLOs for pilot (initial suggestion):
- TTFT median: 60ms (payload <= 256 tokens)
- TTFT p95: 130ms
- Sustained rps envelope: 200 rps; burst up to 1,200 rps for <= 5 minutes
- Success criteria: >= 90% of requests meet p95 SLO during steady-state; no more than two degraded events during bursts (where graceful fallbacks occur)

Attachments: I attached a sample CSV template for the load profile and a one-page pilot-runbook.

If that aligns, we will send a short pilot statement of work and a DocuSign for a technical pilot (no commercial commitment).

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.ai

--

Date: 2027-08-22T18:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: InstaLedger TTFT probing and chunk cadence alignment

Thanks Marcus — appreciate the tidy recap. Couple clarifications and a small ask from our infra team: 

Clarifications: 
- Targets: The 50–60ms median matches what product is hoping for; p95 <= 130ms is acceptable as a pilot bar.
- Chunk cadence: we *strongly* prefer ~40ms visual cadence for the main UI stream (we're sensitive to perceived latency). If that causes meaningful tail increases we need to know tradeoffs.
- Traffic shape: steady 200 rps is accurate, though our export tooling can cause short spikes to ~1,200 rps for 1–3 minutes. These are short but frequent (a few times/day).

Infra ask: Can Redwood confirm whether prefix/KV caching is an option for identical prompt prefixes? We have many repeated small prompts and caching could be a big win on cost/TTFT. Also send any guidance on connection timeouts for SSE vs WebSocket (our load balancer has defaults we can change).

I'll upload a small sample of real payloads to the CSV you attached (send a link if you prefer Drive). Ops contact (copied) will coordinate service account creation once we agree on a pilot window.

—Sam
Sam Lee
Head of Product, InstaLedger
sam@instaledger.com

> On 2027-08-22 16:12, Marcus Lin wrote:
> > Call summary (high level):
> > - Goal: make interactive ledger search feel instantaneous...

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>

Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-22T20:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: InstaLedger TTFT probing and chunk cadence alignment

Great — thanks for the fast reply, Sam. Quick answers inline + proposed pilot config.

On caching: yes, we support prefix/KV caching for repeated prompt prefixes at the router layer. It helps a lot for short identical prompts; we'll include a cache policy in the pilot runbook (TTL, key namespace).

Connection behavior: SSE over TLS is our default for streaming with sane keepalive; typical LB keepalive adjustments are: idle_timeout >= 180s and SSE ping every 30s. WebSocket fallback keeps connections open but has slightly higher handshake latency. We'll provide recommended LB settings.

Proposed pilot configuration (actionable):
- Pilot window: 4 hours; steady-state target: 200 rps; burst sequences: 3 bursts of 2 minutes each to 1,200 rps spaced 60 minutes apart.
- Payload profile: prioritize payloads <256 tokens for initial run; will also include a small fraction (~10%) of 300–600 token queries to measure tail behavior.
- Chunk cadence: default to 40ms target cadence; we'll measure packetization overhead and can relax to 60ms if needed.
- Observability: we will provide a real-time dashboard with token-level latency, TTFT, throughput, and a per-request traceback for any degraded events.

Next steps:
1) Sam / Ops: confirm pilot window availability and upload sample CSV (or grant Drive access).
2) We'll send a pilot SOW and a short DocuSign for the technical pilot.
3) Engineering: please provision a temporary service account for Redwood test runs (ops-contact will coordinate).

I'll attach the pilot-runbook and the CSV template again; small doc with the exact probe commands.

Cheers,
Marcus
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.ai

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-23T03:45:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: InstaLedger TTFT probing and chunk cadence alignment

Forwarding a couple of implementation notes from a quick ops read so we have them before the pilot: 

> Key ops notes (internal):
> - Chunk cadence tradeoff: 40ms visual cadence looks great for UX but increases per-token RPC frequency; suggest measuring both 40ms and 60ms during pilot to quantify CPU scheduling overhead.
> - KV-prefix cache: enable for identical short prompts; use conservative TTL (30s) for the pilot to avoid staleness.
> - Priming: consider a short 1–2 token pre-prime in responses to reduce first-byte jitter (packet coalescing effect).
> - Quantization suggestion: run the pilot on the 8-bit quantized variant of the model we proposed — good latencies, modest quality hit; we can evaluate quality regressions in the same run.
> - Networking: ensure TLS keepalives and LB idle_timeout >= 180s; encourage HTTP/2 where possible for SSE fallback compatibility.

I'll stand by to help instrument the dashboards and produce a short runbook note on how we'll flip cache rules if we see staleness.

Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Product Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Pilot acceptance criteria + schedule ask — InstaLedger TTFT probe

Hi Sam — short summary of acceptance criteria and asks so we can lock the window: 

Acceptance criteria (pilot):
- TTFT median <= 75ms and p95 <= 140ms for payloads under 256 tokens during steady-state (200 rps).
- No more than 2 degrade events during burst sequences (we'll define degrade as >250ms TTFT).
- Evidence of prefix/KV cache hit rate reported in the dashboard (we'll track hit/miss).
- Successful SSE streaming with <5% fallback to WebSocket during the run.

Schedule ask: please confirm one 4-hour window next week (preferred windows: Tue 2027-08-29 14:00–18:00 PDT or Wed 2027-08-30 10:00–14:00 PDT). Also: please upload sample payloads to the Drive folder linked here and grant read to engineers@redwood.ai so we can pre-synthesize the load.

Doc: https://docusign.example.com/pilot/IL-2027-08-22-A (pilot SOW)
Drive: https://drive.example.com/drive/folders/instaledger-pilot

If you confirm the window, we'll schedule the instrumentation call 24 hours prior and run a 30-minute smoke test.

Thanks — Priyom
